Enclosure and Structural Designer said about it: The table in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) gives U Value PIR 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin at 100 millimetre and 0.17 watt per square metre kelvin at 120 millimetre, and the comparison in Sandwich Panel Types: PU, PIR, EPS & Rock Wool Compared (E33) states 100 millimetre Polyurethane (PU, foam insulation) reaches about 0.23 watt per square metre kelvin, so I use Polyisocyanurate (PIR, rigid foam insulation) 100 millimetre walls and 120 millimetre roof and floor at about 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin.
Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer said about it: The table in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) gives heat-transfer coefficient 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin at 100 millimetre, which gives 203 watt conduction in the conduction check (E59), and the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) sizes infiltration as air changes times volume times energy per cubic metre, so 4 air changes per day in the 8.64 cubic metre room cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, so averaged door gain near 18 watt is inside my steady budget and your strip curtain holds.
Enclosure and Structural Designer said about it: The module datasheet in PRBS 400W Monocrystalline Photovoltaic Panels | Commercial & High-Performance (E64) lists dimensions 1722 by 1134 by 30 mm and weight 20.5 kg, matched by dimensions 1762 by 1134 by 30 mm and weight 21.5 kg in SolarPeak Pro 400 (E65), giving six-module footprint 11.7 square metres in the panel footprint calc (E69), about a parking space, against a 2.4 m by 1.8 m roof of 4.32 square metres, so the split shade with 2 Photovoltaic (PV, solar-electric panel) modules on the roof gantry plus 4 modules on a separate ground frame on own footings in that same split layout sketch (E70) carries no panel loads into sandwich panels and keeps the vent gap that holds the 203 watt conduction in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32).
Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer said about it: Transmission is 203 watt in the conduction estimate (E41) inside 615 watt staged average in the revised steady-load simulation (E28), with daily 13.2 kilowatt-hour per day in the steady plus staged pull-down estimate (E58), about one household daily use in everyday scale, so 100 millimetre walls with 120 millimetre roof and floor at heat-transfer coefficient 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin from Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) is the insulation requirement.

statements.text: The table in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) gives U Value PIR 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin at 100 millimetre and 0.17 watt per square metre kelvin at 120 millimetre, and the comparison in Sandwich Panel Types: PU, PIR, EPS & Rock Wool Compared (E33) states 100 millimetre Polyurethane (PU, foam insulation) reaches about 0.23 watt per square metre kelvin, so I use Polyisocyanurate (PIR, rigid foam insulation) 100 millimetre walls and 120 millimetre roof and floor at about 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin.

The table in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) gives heat-transfer coefficient 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin at 100 millimetre, which gives 203 watt conduction in the conduction check (E59), and the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) sizes infiltration as air changes times volume times energy per cubic metre, so 4 air changes per day in the 8.64 cubic metre room cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, so averaged door gain near 18 watt is inside my steady budget and your strip curtain holds.

The module datasheet in PRBS 400W Monocrystalline Photovoltaic Panels | Commercial & High-Performance (E64) lists dimensions 1722 by 1134 by 30 mm and weight 20.5 kg, matched by dimensions 1762 by 1134 by 30 mm and weight 21.5 kg in SolarPeak Pro 400 (E65), giving six-module footprint 11.7 square metres in the panel footprint calc (E69), about a parking space, against a 2.4 m by 1.8 m roof of 4.32 square metres, so the split shade with 2 Photovoltaic (PV, solar-electric panel) modules on the roof gantry plus 4 modules on a separate ground frame on own footings in that same split layout sketch (E70) carries no panel loads into sandwich panels and keeps the vent gap that holds the 203 watt conduction in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32).

Transmission is 203 watt in the conduction estimate (E41) inside 615 watt staged average in the revised steady-load simulation (E28), with daily 13.2 kilowatt-hour per day in the steady plus staged pull-down estimate (E58), about one household daily use in everyday scale, so 100 millimetre walls with 120 millimetre roof and floor at heat-transfer coefficient 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin from Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) is the insulation requirement.
